question: Should nix-openclaw keep requiring ByteRover to publish a Nix-packageable artifact, or should the repo expand its runtime-plugin policy for this third-party context-engine package?
rationale: The current behavior matches documented packageability rules, but the reporter has a real third-party context-engine install need that cannot be resolved safely by a narrow bug fix.

options.title: Keep deterministic artifact rule
options.body: Ask ByteRover to publish npm-shrinkwrap.json or bundled runtime dependencies, then document the exact `runtimePluginSources` configuration once that artifact exists.

options.title: Expand arbitrary npm materialization
options.body: Add a maintainer-approved path for unshrinkwrapped third-party npm plugins, accepting the larger dependency-resolution and reproducibility policy surface.

options.title: Relax raw path mixing
options.body: Permit advanced users to combine generated runtime plugin roots with user-owned raw load paths, accepting a less strict single-source-of-truth model.

recommendation.title: Keep deterministic artifact rule
recommendation.body: Ask ByteRover to publish npm-shrinkwrap.json or bundled runtime dependencies, then document the exact `runtimePluginSources` configuration once that artifact exists.

likelyOwner.reason: This is the clearest available owner from the runtimePluginSources feature history and related merged pull request.
